viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
We’ve been busy shipping 🚢 Here’s a recap of the last couple of weeks:

— Gemini 4 Neon, our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows

— Gemini 4 Hydrogen, our model for speed and efficiency in everyday coding and agentic workflows

— Gemini 4 Carbon, our model for your hardest long-horizon projects and deep research

— Genie 4, @GoogleDeepMind’s most realistic interactive world model featuring real-time scene editing and adaptive native audio, now available in Project Genie (with a new creation agent and gallery) and for the first time in the Gemini API and @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, now with native voice editing that lets developers build experiences where users can edit, rephrase, and translate existing text in a single step using just their voice, via the Gemini API in @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini Robotics 2.5, @GoogleDeepMind’s most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date

— AlphaGenome 2, @GoogleDeepMind’s new AI model that zooms in on specific cells to help scientists understand what drives disease

— Stitch Loop, a new @stitchbygoogle experiment from @GoogleLabs that monitors production data and runs continuous loops to improve your designed product until goals are met

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
$IREN 目前的交易价格为 12.50 美元，我真的没想到我们会再次看到这个水平。

在过去的几个月里，我个人看到这种下跌完全摧毁了投资者对公司及其管理层的信心。

显然这并不是 $IREN 独有的。许多高贝塔值人工智能股票最近都被彻底摧毁，但考虑到今年跌幅的严重程度，$IREN 是更极端的例子之一。

在这样的时刻，我认为互联网泡沫时期的亚马逊是一个非常有趣的案例研究。

在 20 世纪 90 年代末，$AMZN 与其他互联网行业一起取得了令人难以置信的增长，在大约两年半的时间里上涨了 70 倍以上。

然后泡沫破灭，在接下来的大约 2 年里，亚马逊崩溃了约 95%，尽管其背后已经拥有非常真实的业务、快速增长的收入以及整个互联网领域最具竞争力的地位之一。

从最终约 0.27 美元的底部，该股今天继续升至 253 美元左右。

这接近 1,000 倍的回报，或者说 25 年来的复合年增长率约为 31.5%。

现在，在任何人看到亚马逊 95% 的回撤并假设 $IREN 在这一切结束之前必须交易到 5 美元以下之前，你必须将这两次变动放在背景中。

股市崩盘前，亚马逊股价已上涨 70 多倍。
从人工智能热潮开始到顶峰，$IREN 上涨了大约 15 倍。

更广泛的互联网市场的估值水平也使得当今的人工智能行业看起来相对便宜，所以我显然并不认为这两种情况是相同的。

这一比较确实表明，当整个行业陷入残酷的困境时，一家基本面强劲的公司的股票会下跌多少。

$IREN 现在从高峰到低谷已经下跌了大约 84%，但当我审视今天的实际业务时，我很难找到任何可以证明这种崩溃的理由。
如果说有什么不同的话，那就是该公司的竞争地位在整个过程中得到了加强。

新合同的经济性不断改善，最近签署的协议达到了管理层几年前只能梦想的水平。

其融资状况也更加强劲。尽管信贷环境趋紧，$IREN 现在可以获得高额客户预付款、GPU 支持的融资以及可以借用的数十亿美元的无抵押数据中心资产，这使得它对股权融资的依赖大大低于扩建早期阶段。

与此同时，对人工智能计算的需求空前高涨。

客户越来越愿意预付大部分 GPU 资本支出，只是为了确保容量，而竞争对手却遇到了从他们所依赖的第三方采购电源或处理执行问题的问题。

这与 $IREN 多年前的定位完全一致。

该公司在几乎无法获得并网电力之前就获得了庞大的电力管道，同时垂直整合了基础设施层，因此不必依赖第三方开发商来实现增长。

在执行和权力获取正在成为整个行业瓶颈的时期，我希望拥有这种设置。

对于那些认为 $AMZN 比较幸存者偏差的人来说，当然绝大多数互联网股票从未恢复。然而，他们中的大多数人不应该这样做。

高贝塔值“.com”市场的很大一部分由那些只有好故事的公司组成，它们希望最终能够出现可行的业务，而市场无论如何都以疯狂的估值奖励它们。

亚马逊之所以能脱颖而出，是因为该股背后有一个真正的商业引擎，而且即使股价暴跌 95%，该引擎仍继续变得更强。

这是我发现与 $IREN 相当的部分。

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

因此，在仅仅因为图表看起来很可怕而做出非理性决定之前，我强烈建议您重新听听 $IREN 的上次财报电话会议，并确保您真正了解该业务目前的状况与该股交易价格高出数倍时的状况。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

事后看来，那些白痴才是把股票暴跌和企业崩溃混为一谈的人……

top_three.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
top_three.title_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
top_three.author: Lauren Feiner
top_three.content_snippet:
President Donald Trump promised to put a “tremendous tax” on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, an
top_three.summary_en: U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed a 'tremendous tax' on American companies that construct AI data centers outside the country. This policy initiative is framed as a matter of national security, aiming to prevent the offshore migration of critical computing infrastructure and ensure the sovereignty of the domestic AI supply chain.
paragraphs: President Donald Trump promised to put a “tremendous tax” on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, and it was very destructive to our country. It’s where we started going behind.” Should the US allow data centers to be built outside of the country, Trump warned, “China will take them all.”

Trump didn’t share many details behind the plan, and apparently was floating the proposal publicly for the first time. “I don’t know if that’s a breaking story. But I haven’t even said that to my people,” Trump said, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. “But I’m telling them now. They’re here. Many of them are here.”

Trump’s promise could be difficult to fulfill with a new Democratic majority Congress being sworn in within a couple of months. Even members of his own party recognize that the data center buildout has become an unpopular issue across the board. With states installing moratoriums and new restrictions on data center proposals, companies may be forced to look outside of the country, but Trump’s threat is an attempt to make that a less attractive alternative.

top_three.summary_en: Google has integrated the 'Computer Use' feature into its Gemini Mac app, allowing the AI to simulate mouse clicks, keyboard inputs, and menu navigation within isolated background windows. This enables the autonomous execution of multi-step tasks across local files and web applications while allowing users to maintain foreground workflow continuity.
paragraphs: Google now lets Gemini handle Mac tasks in the background. The new "Computer Use"feature in the Gemini Mac app completes multistep tasks across local files, desktop apps, and websites. Google says users simply describe a goal, and Gemini clicks, types, and navigates menus and forms. Everything runs in an isolated background window with a live chat preview, keeping the screen and cursor free for uninterrupted work.

Users choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause anytime, and approve key actions beforehand. Google's examples include batch-editing photos and 3D scenes, filling out shipping forms from local PDFs, and building presentations.
Computer Use rolls out in English in the US today, and the Gemini Mac app is available to download. OpenAI has also focused on Computer Use recently, pulling well ahead with its Astra model.

linked_tweets.author: Chubby♨️
linked_tweets.content_zh:
今天创造了历史。人类将在回顾 2026 年时思考：这是我们跨过的门槛，从那一刻起，每个人的未来都将永远改变。

人们可能在 2025 年底通过 Claude Code 第一次感觉到事情正在发生变化，当时代理人工智能对他们来说变得真正有形。 2026 年上半年，事情加速发展。模型发布越来越频繁，大家都能感受到模型之间的差距和改进越来越明显。然而到了2026年下半年，却出现了质的飞跃。这不再只是模型变得更好了。人工智能产生的见解、结果、产出和科学解决方案变得更加令人印象深刻，今天它们可能已经达到了绝对的顶峰。

OpenAI 率先解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，这是人类在很长一段时间内未能解决的千年奖问题。几周后，他们发表了 300 多个开放数学问题的结果，其中许多问题几十年来都没有得到解决。整个科学界都惊呆了，震惊不已。但今天 Anthropic 更进一步。 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，几乎肯定证明了黎曼猜想。这实在是难以用言语来形容，令人难以置信，深不可测。我想说，今天是超级智能的证明。 167 年来一直没有解决的最伟大的数学问题之一，数学和科学的圣杯，即使不是最伟大的，也已经陨落了。接下来，每个人都应该清楚，所有其他问题也会随之下降。

我们知道，人工智能模型的发展不断向前发展，而这只是迈向更好模型的第一步。如果黎曼假设今天已经得到证明，那么根本不知道更好的模型会解决什么问题。达里奥·阿莫迪表示，人工智能很可能会治愈疾病，甚至可能治愈所有疾病。尽管这是两个不同的科学学科，但这些突破的意义表明，这种情况变得越来越有可能。 2026 年将作为一个转折点载入人类历史，奇点变得有形的那一刻。 2027 年将是奇点以全力和全面影响力进入现实的一年。

我感到震惊和兴奋，不知道该怎么想。但内心深处却感到喜悦。

这一天对我们所有人来说都是最美好的日子之一。
linked_tweets.content_en:
History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the future changed for everyone, forever.

People probably first sensed that something was shifting in late 2025 with Claude Code, when agentic AI became truly tangible for them. In the first half of 2026, things picked up speed. Model releases became more frequent, and everyone could feel the gaps between models and the improvements becoming more and more tangible. In the second half of 2026, however, there was a qualitative leap. It was no longer just the models getting better. It was the insights, the results, the outputs, the scientific solutions produced with AI that became more impressive, and today they have probably reached their absolute peak.

OpenAI led the way and solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a Millennium Prize Problem that humans had failed to solve for a very, very long time. A few weeks later, they published results on more than 300 open mathematical problems, many of which had also gone unsolved for decades. The entire scientific world was stunned, frozen in shock. But today Anthropic went a step further. Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, has almost certainly proven the Riemann Hypothesis. This is, and it’s hard to put into words, incredible and unfathomable. Today, I would say, is the proof of superintelligence. One of the greatest mathematical problems, if not the greatest, unsolved for 167 years, the holy grail of mathematics and science, has fallen. And it follows, and this should be clear to everyone, that all other problems will fall too.

We know that the development of AI models keeps moving forward relentlessly, and that this is just one step on the path to ever better models. And if the Riemann Hypothesis has already been proven today, there is simply no telling what even better models will solve. Dario Amodei said that AI will in all likelihood cure diseases, perhaps even all diseases. And although these are two different scientific disciplines, the significance of these breakthroughs shows that this is becoming more and more likely. 2026 will go down in human history as a turning point, the moment the singularity became tangible. And 2027 will be the year the singularity breaks into reality with full force and full impact.

I am in shock and excitement and I don't know what to think. But deep inside if feel joy. 

This day is one of the best days ever for all of us.

news.title: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
news.title_en: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
Google now lets Gemini handle Mac tasks in the background. The new "Computer Use"feature in the Gemini Mac app completes multistep tasks across local files, desktop apps, and websites. Google says users simply describe a goal, and Gemini clicks, types, and navigates menus and forms. Everything runs in an isolated background window with a live chat preview, keeping the screen and cursor free for uninterrupted work.

Users choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause anytime,
news.summary_en: Google has integrated the 'Computer Use' feature into its Gemini Mac app, allowing the AI to simulate mouse clicks, keyboard inputs, and menu navigation within isolated background windows. This enables the autonomous execution of multi-step tasks across local files and web applications while allowing users to maintain foreground workflow continuity.
paragraphs: Google now lets Gemini handle Mac tasks in the background. The new "Computer Use"feature in the Gemini Mac app completes multistep tasks across local files, desktop apps, and websites. Google says users simply describe a goal, and Gemini clicks, types, and navigates menus and forms. Everything runs in an isolated background window with a live chat preview, keeping the screen and cursor free for uninterrupted work.

Users choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause anytime, and approve key actions beforehand. Google's examples include batch-editing photos and 3D scenes, filling out shipping forms from local PDFs, and building presentations.
Computer Use rolls out in English in the US today, and the Gemini Mac app is available to download. OpenAI has also focused on Computer Use recently, pulling well ahead with its Astra model.

news.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
news.title_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
news.author: Lauren Feiner
news.content_snippet:
President Donald Trump promised to put a “tremendous tax” on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, an
news.summary_en: U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed a 'tremendous tax' on American companies that construct AI data centers outside the country. This policy initiative is framed as a matter of national security, aiming to prevent the offshore migration of critical computing infrastructure and ensure the sovereignty of the domestic AI supply chain.
paragraphs: President Donald Trump promised to put a “tremendous tax” on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, and it was very destructive to our country. It’s where we started going behind.” Should the US allow data centers to be built outside of the country, Trump warned, “China will take them all.”

Trump didn’t share many details behind the plan, and apparently was floating the proposal publicly for the first time. “I don’t know if that’s a breaking story. But I haven’t even said that to my people,” Trump said, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. “But I’m telling them now. They’re here. Many of them are here.”

Trump’s promise could be difficult to fulfill with a new Democratic majority Congress being sworn in within a couple of months. Even members of his own party recognize that the data center buildout has become an unpopular issue across the board. With states installing moratoriums and new restrictions on data center proposals, companies may be forced to look outside of the country, but Trump’s threat is an attempt to make that a less attractive alternative.

news.summary_en: Intelligence firm Strider Technologies identified that Alice Huang and her associates built a complex network utilizing $3.6 billion in Chinese government funding for data centers equipped with Nvidia AI chips. The investigation reveals that these entities maintain deep ties to Chinese military contractors and the Ministry of State Security, posing significant compliance risks regarding the diversion of restricted hardware into military research.
paragraphs: Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal, has extensive ties through her family and associates to China’s defense industry, according to an independent research firm and corporate filings reviewed by The New York Times.

The findings show a web of relationships, most of them indirect, linking Ms. Huang’s family and companies that acquired Nvidia chips to Chinese state-owned defense contractors that supply the People’s Liberation Army.

The nature of those relationships, including the vital question of whether Nvidia chips ended up being used to support Chinese military projects, remains murky. But the revelations, along with an investigation by The Times published on Wednesday, underscore how the Chinese effort to acquire access to the computing power of Nvidia’s chips is intertwined with Beijing’s desire to harness artificial intelligence to bolster its military capabilities.

That outcome has long been feared by U.S. national security officials, given that the technology could help China develop more sophisticated weapons, carry out cyberattacks and integrate A.I. into the battlefield.

A confidential analysis by Strider Technologies, an independent intelligence firm that employs former intelligence officers and experts on China and specializes in corporate intelligence, shows that about $3.6 billion in Chinese government money flowed through companies associated with Ms. Huang’s family or associates. The government money funded technology projects, including data centers that received Nvidia chips.
The New York Times reviewed the Strider findings. Many of the corporate ties revealed by Strider were independently confirmed by The Times.

The Times reported last month that U.S. officials believe Ms. Huang, a Chinese citizen also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese intelligence asset who was providing information to the Ministry of State Security. The Strider Technologies analysis and the review of corporate filings by The Times show that she; her sister, Huang Yu; and an investor named Kang Wei, who was Alice Huang’s business partner and often introduced as her husband, are tied to a web of companies that connect official Nvidia partners, which can buy advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, to state- and military-linked projects.
Nvidia’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, stepped down as the company’s chief executive after acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, who is no relation.

Companies in the Huang family’s network co-own a cybersecurity venture with an arm of China’s main military-electronics conglomerate, lease Nvidia-powered servers financed by an affiliate of its largest military aircraft maker and in one case share a parent company with a maker of radar and missile components.

Two companies that have partnerships with Nvidia, Megaspeed and Century Litong, are connected to Ms. Huang. Ms. Huang ran Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center firm that is under investigation by the Justice Department for smuggling advanced chips into China. Megaspeed has said Ms. Huang, whose involvement with Mr. Huang corresponded with a period when it was acquiring large numbers of Nvidia chips, no longer works for the company.

Ms. Huang’s family members had prominent roles and significant investments in the data center firm that founded Century Litong, which is based in Shanghai and rents out computing power to major Chinese companies and military contractors. The family members include Ms. Huang’s sister and Mr. Kang.

U.S. officials are also working to learn more about Ms. Huang and her efforts to help supply chips to data centers. The nature and extent of her ties to the P.L.A. and the companies it controls are a focus of that work, according to people briefed on the American efforts.

The ties are complex and often indirect. The research does not show whether the P.L.A. used computing power in the data centers that the family’s companies helped build. But it shows how deeply Ms. Huang and her family are intertwined with the Chinese state, and the inextricable connections between China’s tech industry and its military.

“Beijing has spent years building these networks that reach deep into Western economies,” said Greg Levesque, the chief executive of Strider. “Follow the money and, too often, you find the P.L.A. at the end of it.”

Mr. Levesque said China was exploiting more Western technology, capital and talent than ever before to build its defense industrial base. “This is happening on a scale we simply weren’t seeing a few years ago,” he said.
Nvidia declined to comment. Megaspeed did not respond to a request for comment. Ms. Huang could not be reached for comment.

From late last year into early this year, Century Litong appears to have been one of only a few sources able to supply Nvidia chips to China at the vast scale needed for its A.I. build-out, according to Strider.

Those chips were key to building the data centers that drive China’s A.I. development. Investigators are trying to determine how many of the chips that were used in those data centers were banned under U.S. export controls and, in essence, smuggled into the country. Companies controlled by Ms. Huang and her relatives were instrumental in supplying the chips, Strider found.
“Essentially, those entities worked around the controls to continue to meet the chip demands of the customers they already had, including at new data centers,” Mr. Levesque said.

On Thursday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee took the unusual step of releasing confidential information on Nvidia’s license applications to legally sell H200 chips to Chinese firms. The list showed that Nvidia had sought permission to sell more than 40,000 H200s to the Hong Kong subsidiary of Century Litong.
An Nvidia spokesman said that, despite receiving some licenses, it had already stopped shipping H200s to China, and Nvidia had not and would not ship to that firm.

Century Litong has said it has no business dealings with Ms. Huang. But the company was founded in 2023 by Century Longteng, a data center operator that was then 27 percent owned by an investment firm controlled by Ms. Huang’s sister. Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s presumed husband, had been Century Longteng’s executive director since February 2022, according to Strider.

In 2023, Jiangsu Lettall Electronic, a Shanghai-listed maker of metal parts for flat-screen TVs, bought 90 percent of Century Litong, and owned all of it by 2024. Lettall also owns 80 percent of Nanjing Jinning Microwave, a maker of components that Lettall has said are used in Chinese radar and missile systems. Strider said Jinning’s parts go into the P.L.A.’s DF-series missiles, including intercontinental ballistic missiles and anti-ship “carrier killers,” as well as the J-20 stealth fighter plane.
China’s defense industry wants advanced A.I. chips to design better missiles and build other military software, experts have said.

Lettall did not respond to an emailed request for comment. Asked about Ms. Huang’s network of companies and their efforts to acquire chips, the spokesman for the Chinese Embassy in Washington said he was not familiar with the situation. “We have made clear more than once our principled position on U.S. chip exports to China,” said the spokesman, Liu Chang.

Century Litong delivered servers containing Nvidia’s H800 chips to a supercomputing center in Shanghai in October 2023, according to Strider. It is unclear where Century Litong obtained those chips, but they may have been obtained legally, since U.S. restrictions on the sale of the H800 to China did not go into effect until that same month.

Century Litong now runs servers at the Shanghai supercomputing center under a lease of about $54 million from a leasing arm of the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, China’s state aerospace and defense conglomerate.

Century Litong’s reach extends far beyond the Chinese A.I. giant Tencent. When Lettall bought into the company in 2023, it said all of Century Litong’s computing business would be housed in two places: the Tencent center in Shanghai and a data center in Shenzhen.

The Shenzhen center was built for the cloud unit of Huawei, the Chinese telecom giant that has long been under sanctions by the United States over national security concerns. Huawei awarded the project in 2022 to a company controlled by Century Longteng, according to corporate filings.

Century Litong’s customers have also included a unit of China Electronics Technology Group, or C.E.T.C., a state-owned military electronics maker. The United States has included C.E.T.C. on its list of companies that it publicly identifies as doing work with the Chinese military, banning the firm from doing work with Pentagon suppliers.
Another Century Litong partner is Hangjin Technology, a listed company whose subsidiaries make chips for China’s military.

Until last December, Hangjin controlled Chaoqing, an Nvidia partner whose website once listed High-Flyer, the hedge fund behind the Chinese A.I. start-up DeepSeek, as a partner. Others on the list included the military-linked Zhejiang Lab and its co-founder, Alibaba.

DeepSeek has attracted attention for its cutting-edge A.I. models. But lawmakers in the United States have also accused it of presenting national security risks, and the federal government has banned employees from using it. The Information earlier reported ties between Ms. Huang’s network and DeepSeek.
Hangjin did not respond to an emailed request for comment. It has said it does no business with DeepSeek.
subheadings: The Trail to Huawei and DeepSeek

news.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
news.title_en: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
news.author: Grace Huckins
news.content_snippet:

news.summary_en: Nonprofit evaluation group METR has updated its time-horizon plot for AI capabilities, indicating that models show exponential growth in verifiable tasks like coding and mathematics, but lag in judgment-based tasks that lack automated verification. The report highlights the technological bottleneck in applying reinforcement learning to complex, open-ended research decisions, a capability critical for future autonomous R&D.
paragraphs: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.

The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , due to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.

The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than the tasks in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. We know how to teach neural networks how to do verifiable tasks: Researchers have the systems attempt the task many times, strengthen the neural pathways that contribute to success, and weaken the pathways that contribute to failures. That’s why AI systems have become so good at coding and math, two domains where it’s possible to determine automatically whether a solution does or doesn’t work.

It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential to AI systems automating research and development.

And AI research and development is an especially hot topic right now. Parts of the AI community are still reeling from a different, heavily redacted METR report from earlier this month weeks ago, which claimed that AI might be speeding up the pace of AI capabilities progress at Anthropic by a factor of two. That report sparked fears that the company (which just had a blockbuster IPO) could soon achieve full recursive self-improvement, a regime in which AI systems autonomously design their own successors with no human involvement.

METR researchers have worked to incorporate some of these fuzzier, judgment-laden tasks that could be most relevant to AI research and development into their new suite. In one task, they ask models to design new AI evaluations that METR could use in its research and then have human METR employees score the results. Even though the most advanced models are now better than almost every human at software engineering, here they fall short: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research.

In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments. This task is intended to capture the extent to which models can exercise good judgment—though METR writes in the report that employees disagree about the extent to which the task is relevant for AI R&D automation. On this task, too, models fell short of human performance.

Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks—and even more so to determine what these scores mean—experts I spoke with appreciate that METR is incorporating new types of evaluations into their work. “We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative,” says Sayash Kapoor, a computer scientist and incoming professor at UC Berkeley. “Trying to push the envelope of the space of evaluations is a welcome change.”

Kapoor says he wasn’t surprised to see that models fall short of performance on more open-ended tasks, such as designing an AI evaluation—in a preprint from August , he and his collaborators reported that AI models are not yet able to reproduce human computer science research on their own. And in a Wednesday blog post, OpenAI reported that its models don’t do as well on the real-world tasks its employees ask them to do as they do on the easier, more verifiable tasks in METR’s original task suite.

Still, people disagree about how to interpret current performance differences on easily verifiable and hard-to-verify tasks, Kapoor says. Though he thinks that research taste—the ability to choose promising research questions, hypotheses, and experiments—will prove a major bottleneck to AI R&D automation, others contend that models trained on easy-to-verify tasks will eventually be able to successfully complete open-ended tasks as well. And progress on verifiable tasks doesn’t seem to be slowing down.

Even if the models do lag behind human performance on open-ended tasks right now, the new report suggests that they might be getting better. Some of the newest models, such as Opus 5.5, tend to achieve what METR calls “borderline above the bar” performance on the evaluation design tasks—not yet usable for METR’s research, but promising. Just a year ago, every model was scoring in the “clearly below the bar” category.

But because these open-ended and judgment-heavy tasks are so tough to design and score, METR includes few of them in its report, and that makes it difficult to predict whether and how models might continue to progress in these areas. “The improvement we observe, I think that does tell us something for the current moment,” says Najoung Kim, a linguist and computer scientist at Boston University. “I’m not sure just yet how to think about how it would extrapolate.”

Matt Putz, a member of the technical staff at METR, says that predicting progress on these kinds of tasks is likely to remain difficult. “By their nature, hard-to-verify or judgment-laden tasks are much harder to study, and especially to quantify,” he said in an email. “Ultimately, I don’t think we’ll be able to establish trends as clean and robust as for the easy-to-specify [tasks].”

In general, METR is clearly butting up against the practical difficulties of testing AI performance on difficult and underspecified tasks—precisely the tasks most relevant to AI R&D automation. METR’s time horizon plots score task difficulty by evaluating how long it would take a human to complete the task, and for the original plot they measured this quantity by actually having people try each task.

In the new report, however, the completion times are mostly estimates, because paying people to complete tasks that might take hundreds of hours, or that only a few experts are qualified to complete, is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming. Other tasks have more specific shortcomings—for example, for the philosophical argument task, just one person rated most of the arguments, and agents are judged by how well they agree with that particular individual. It’s possible that the scores would change if more experts were surveyed—but that, too, is time consuming.

It’s still early days for evaluating models on tasks that are hard to validate or require judgment. And while the experts I spoke with see the inclusion of these tasks in METR’s newest time horizon plot as a clear step in the right direction, they agree that we are still far from achieving any definitive answers about whether, and how quickly, automated AI R&D might be coming. “This move towards open-ended tasks is promising,” Kapoor says. But, he adds, “there is just such a lot more to be done to actually get a fuller understanding.”

news.summary_en: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that humans must maintain control over military decisions involving artificial intelligence, prohibiting autonomous 'superintelligence' (SI) in major military actions, as confirmed by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The leaders also engaged in robust discussions regarding nuclear non-proliferation, trade policy, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, culminating in a joint declaration emphasizing that nuclear war must never be fought.
paragraphs: Reporting the Changing World

US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed that humans should always be involved in military decisions made by artificial intelligence, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday.

“I think it was very important that the President Trump, and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent told CNBC, using the term “SI,” or superintelligence, for the technology.
Bessent said there was also “very robust discussion on what can be done in terms of containing the growth of nuclear weapons.”
He said the leaders held “a robust discussion on trade policy, AI,” and discussed the Russia-Ukraine war with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump, Xi and Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. In a joint declaration after the meeting, the three leaders reaffirmed that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.”

news.author: Robert Hart and Emma Roth

paragraphs: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’s most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world’s best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval already unleashed by OpenAI’s previous, often inelegant forays into the field.

Alpöge’s solution has yet to be verified independently. Anthropic has not commented or involved itself in Alpöge’s announcement. In a document on his website, Alpöge says he texted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about the solution “late Sunday night” and suggests he held off publication until after the company’s IPO on Thursday.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of seven Millennium Prize problems, which are widely considered some of the most formidable open challenges in mathematics. First proposed in 1859, the Riemann hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and how zeroes of a function are involved. It’s regarded as one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics.
A statement on Alpöge’s website says Claude was integral to developing the proof:

The Verge reached out to Anthropic but didn’t immediately hear back. Anthropic said it was working on the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude in August, but noted at the time: “We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis.”

Alpöge’s solution, presented in Lean, has only been published on his website and has not yet been publicly accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which administers the Millennium Prize and offers a $1 million bounty for each problem solved. Under the institute’s rules, a proposed solution must be published and withstand at least two years of scrutiny before it can be considered for the prize, during which time it must have “received general acceptance in the global mathematics community.”

In the quarter-century since the prize was established, only one problem has been officially solved: The Poincaré conjecture, a topological problem concerning three-dimensional spheres. In September, OpenAI claimed to have cracked another, the Navier-Stokes problem, which concerns the flow of fluids.

OpenAI said it pursued Navier-Stokes after hearing rumors that rival researchers were closing in on a solution. Alpöge had been working on the problem with New York University mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster. Buckmaster claimed OpenAI produced a solution for Navier-Stokes using the route he and Alpöge were working on with OpenAI’s Codex and Claude.

OpenAI spent millions of dollars and deployed 10,000 agents in the attempt. The result is widely considered credible, though it has yet to receive formal recognition. But the achievement has been marred by allegations of questionable research practices, including claims it used unpublished work from mathematicians who had shared their research with its AI tools. OpenAI has strongly denied wrongdoing, but this has done little to quell the uproar.

Though most of the spotlight has been on OpenAI’s movement in math, Alpöge said in July that he solved the Jacobean conjecture using Claude. The deluge of findings has left mathematicians scrambling to digest the material and figure out where they belong in what is rapidly becoming a profoundly different mathematical landscape.

news.title_en: Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings shows AI-exposed roles in China fell 10 percentage points faster than others
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
An analysis of 10 million job postings by Bloomberg suggests that AI is putting additional pressure on China's already weak labor market. Entry-level workers and the creative industry in particular are reportedly already feeling the shift.

China's labor market has struggled for years with a sluggish economy, and AI now appears to be making things worse. According to a Bloomberg News analysis of nearly 10 million online job postings between July 2021 and June 2025, listings for jobs highly expos
news.summary_en: of nearly 10 million job postings reveals that AI is significantly disrupting China's labor market, disproportionately affecting entry-level and creative roles. Vulnerable positions have seen a demand decline 10 percentage points sharper than non-impacted roles, with research from ShanghaiTech University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences confirming structural shifts including role consolidation and quiet staff reductions at major internet firms.
paragraphs: An analysis of 10 million job postings by Bloomberg suggests that AI is putting additional pressure on China's already weak labor market. Entry-level workers and the creative industry in particular are reportedly already feeling the shift.

China's labor market has struggled for years with a sluggish economy, and AI now appears to be making things worse. According to a Bloomberg News analysis of nearly 10 million online job postings between July 2021 and June 2025, listings for jobs highly exposed to AI fell about 10 percentage points more than listings for less affected roles.

Bloomberg found that the total number of online job postings halved in the three years after June 2022, a starting point shortly before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and Chinese models like DeepSeek and ByteDance's Doubao rose to prominence. In nearly every industry, the decline hit jobs harder when their tasks overlapped heavily with AI capabilities, as measured by an index from Peking University. Bloomberg acknowledges, however, that the pure AI effect cannot be isolated with certainty because the broader economic slowdown may have hit office jobs disproportionately on its own.
### Chinese studies back up the findings

Two independent Chinese studies reached similar conclusions, according to Bloomberg. Data scientist Chen Qin of ShanghaiTech University analyzed 116 million online job postings and estimates that AI caused a net loss of 5.2% in new hires between 2023 and early 2026.

A study involving the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences goes even further, finding 21% fewer online job postings and 4% lower average wages. Bloomberg Economics estimates that roughly 70 million workers in China are at risk from AI disruption, compared with about 45 million in the US.

Chinese tech companies avoid citing AI openly as a reason for layoffs because they fear backlash from the government and the public, Bloomberg reports. Companies including Xiaomi, Meituan, and Alibaba's travel unit Fliggy have denied mass layoffs. Employees at large firms, however, have reported waves of cuts since spring that affected up to 30% of some departments.

Previously separate roles are also merging, according to Bloomberg. One Beijing-based internet company reportedly combined programming, design, and testing so that a single person using AI would take on the work of up to six people. Job postings from Tencent for an "AI Design Engineer"and from BlueFocus for an "AI Director"point in the same direction.
### AI micro-dramas are replacing film crews

According to Bloomberg, the shift is even more dramatic in Chinese micro-dramas, 90-second soap operas made for smartphones. Since the launch of new AI video generators like ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 in February, production time and costs have plummeted. Official data show that more than 90% of the 430,000 micro-dramas produced in the first eight months of 2026 were AI-generated. Linying Studio near Hangzhou, which opened only in late 2023, now sits mostly empty, and actresses like 26-year-old Zhang Ziqi report losing more than a third of their income.

According to the World Bank, China created only 21 million net new jobs in the five years through 2024, while youth unemployment reached nearly 19% over the summer. At the same time, more than 70 million college graduates are crowding into the job market, leading many to turn to retraining programs. China's leadership announced a nationwide survey on AI's labor-market effects in June, called for a "prudent pace,"and overhauled about a third of degree programs. Former central bank adviser Cai Fang nonetheless warns that the current situation is only a "temporary lull"before a bigger AI shock.

Similar patterns among entry-level workers are emerging outside China, though under different economic conditions. Stanford University researchers analyzed millions of US payroll records and found that employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in highly AI-exposed occupations has declined 13% in relative terms since late 2022, while experienced workers held steady. The decline was limited to occupations where AI directly automates tasks, which the researchers attribute to models mainly replacing formal textbook knowledge rather than hands-on experience.

In Australia, too, an analysis by the central bank found weaker employment figures and higher joblessness among 15- to 24-year-olds in highly exposed fields compared with older workers. Like Bloomberg, however, the bank cautioned against drawing causal conclusions too quickly, citing possible business-cycle and remote-work effects.

Anthropic PBC shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors’ faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.

Shares in the company behind the Claude chatbot plunged as low as $87.26 each in early trading in its second day as a public company, trimming the gain from the IPO price of $83 to as little as 5.1%. The stock popped just after opening on Thursday, briefly lifting Anthropic’s market value above Amazon.com Inc.’s, before beginning its slide.

The drop came at the same time as the so-called over-allotment option, also known as a greenshoe, was exercised, allowing the underwriting banks to sell additional shares. The over-allotment lifted the total raised by Anthropic and the co-founders selling shares in the offering to $119.5 billion, with $93.5 billion in the IPO and $26 billion from the concurrent private placement.

The trading gives Anthropic a market value of about $1.5 trillion, ranking it among the 15 biggest publicly traded companies in the world. Stocks were roiled by a selloff that spread from Asia to the US, with the Nasdaq 100 Index falling 1.5% and the S&P 500 Index sinking 0.5%.
“There’s a buyers’ strike for Anthropic as well as the wider AI and tech trade,” according to Emmanuel Valavanis of Forte Securities.

“There are many clients who appear to have been left without allocations and, having been left out of the party, aren’t prepared to pick up the pieces from the hangover. With no skin in the game, and no index considerations for risk of relative performance, investors can sit on the sidelines and wait for longer term price discovery rather than risk getting caught out.”

Anthropic’s IPO made history not only because of its size, but also because the company is the first frontier AI model maker to go public. The trading represents a test of whether investors have appetite for companies pioneering the technology itself, rather than the tools to develop it such as chips and data centers. It also sets up a debut for rival OpenAI, which isn’t planning to go public before 2027.

The IPO delivered outsize returns to its backers and pushing up the combined wealth of its seven founders to $166 billion. The fundraise eclipsed the record set in June by SpaceX’s IPO, which ultimately totaled $86.2 billion. Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks earned a record $550 million in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.

“We are impressed by the wealth creation this company is generating, in a matter of a few years and with reasonable free cash flow burn,” said Raphael Thuin, head of capital markets strategies at Tikehau Capital.
“To get exposed to AI though, we tend to favor more diversified businesses, and in any case we would like to see the post IPO volatility fade before engaging further.”

Anthropic won over investors with a focus on enterprise customers, propelling its run-rate revenue — a measure annualized from a shorter period — to $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, its regulatory filings show.

Claude Code, the company’s coding agent for software developers, is widely adopted in the industry and has even been used by NASA engineers, the filing shows. Anthropic has more than 11,900 customers delivering $100,000 of revenue each on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September, up from about 1,500 in 2025.

Investors considering taking stakes may decide to wait out the market turmoil first. The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s so-called fear gauge, spiked to more than 29 on Friday morning, well above the level where companies typically consider the market welcoming to IPOs.
“We would look at buying in the open market if the stock get close or even below the IPO price,” said Olivier David, a fund manager at Vega IS.

Anthropic’s listing joins companies linked to AI that have pushed US IPO volume to an all-time high. Including Anthropic, first time stock sales raised $258 billion this year, beating 2021’s $195 billion haul, excluding financial vehicles such as blank-check firms, data compiled by Bloomberg show. paragraphs: After Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google launched their own AI agents, Apple is now building one too - while making it harder for rivals to access its devices. According to a job listing, Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead the project as a rival to Muse, Dots, Duet, and Grok Bots. Privacy is expected to be central to the new agent, with permission models and sandboxing (protected test environments).

According to Bloomberg, the agent could arrive as early as late next year, though it remains in an early stage. Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, is pushing software chief Craig Federighi toward a bolder AI strategy, the report says. After many delays, the company recently rolled out generative AI features for Siri. The road to that release was marked by internal rifts and staff departures.

Meanwhile, macOS 27.3 now requires 14 steps instead of four for users to let third-party agents like ChatGPT control their Macs. Apple says the change protects users, though some AI companies and users see it as an effort to slow down competitors, Bloomberg reports.

news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
Nvidia is nearing a deal to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million. That's according to three people familiar with the talks told The Information. The deal also includes performance bonuses for the more than 30 employees at the two-year-old San Francisco Bay Area startup.

news.summary_en: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million, including full-time integration of founders Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. Inception specializes in diffusion-based language models, such as Mercury 3, which refine responses globally rather than token-by-token. This acquisition is designed to enhance Nvidia's Nemotron open-source lineup and accelerate its physical simulation capabilities for robotics.
paragraphs: Nvidia is nearing a deal to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million. That's according to three people familiar with the talks told The Information. The deal also includes performance bonuses for the more than 30 employees at the two-year-old San Francisco Bay Area startup.

Inception builds language models using the diffusion process known from image generation. Rather than generating responses token by token like the conventional models behind ChatGPT and Claude, they refine a full response step by step. The startup most recently released Mercury 3.

The acquisition aims to bolster Nvidia's open-source Nemotron models and physical models for robots, helping it compete with OpenAI and Anthropic as both build their own inference chips. Palantir and US government agencies already use Nemotron as an alternative to Chinese models. Talks began before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and after Microsoft expressed interest. Inception co-founders and professors Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov are expected to join Nvidia full time. Neither company initially commented.
We covered Inception's approach alongside 40 other neolabs in our latest AI Radar #5.

paragraphs: There was a dayslong Outlook outage. A nationwide ground stop for only the second time in 25 years. Banks seemed to suddenly stop working. Even iCloud couldn’t stay up and running. This week, it felt like the technological world simply collapsed. And it felt like this might be the beginning of something even bigger.

On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David go through the week’s many calamities, and try to explain both what happened in each case — which was generally much milder than the conspiracy theories would have you believe — and why all these small issues might still add up to something worth worrying about. In a world filled with more AI and fewer humans, we’re going to see new kinds of problems and often struggle to find the fixes.

After that, the hosts discuss the latest in the Jensen Huang / Nvidia scandal, which is increasingly less about affairs and more about the allegedly very big business of illegally smuggling chips to China. Huang will not be back as Nvidia CEO anytime soon, no matter what a bunch of X users want, and the fallout of his exit seems likely to only increase.

Simultaneously, the company closed a $26 billion private placement involving major tech entities like AMD, Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia, bringing total gross proceeds to $119.5 billion.
paragraphs: Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release on Friday.
The artificial intelligence company raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and net an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

Anthropic said it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe."

Shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in pre-market trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

In addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic said Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry plans for a multi-trillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.
The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone"in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but said there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

"For us, it's like one stop on the journey,"Daniela Amodei said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'"

paragraphs: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar globally on its Desktop Search homepage, making AI search even easier to access. Announced on X by Google Search VP Robby Stein, the feature lets users easily find and reopen recent AI searches. Sitting on the left side of the AI Mode interface, it lets users start new threads, search existing ones, create notebooks, and open recent queries and settings.

Stein said people are increasingly asking Google Search questions that a single query can't answer. In testing, the sidebar significantly helped users make progress and keep researching across the web by making it easier to pick up right where they left off. The update also pushes Google's shift toward an AI answer engine.

Google is also rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode worldwide. These searches don't use prior context, aren't saved to history, and don't affect future recommendations. Once closed, they're gone, Stein said.

news.summary_en: Uber has launched the 'Uber Kids' pilot program in Austin, Nashville, and Madison, lowering the minimum ride-hailing age to 10. The service mandates parental onboarding, real-time video monitoring, PIN verification, and GPS-based off-course detection, while offering participating high-rated drivers a $7 premium per trip.
paragraphs: Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities as the company tests whether there’s a market for shuttling tweens without an adult by their side. The program, called Uber Kids, launched quietly over the past few weeks in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin.

The program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base. Uber is describing this as a limited pilot program, which means it may never expand beyond these cities or even exist by next year. But if successful, it could open up a potentially lucrative market for Uber: busy families with active kids.

The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers. Parents or guardians are the only ones who can order a ride for their child, which they can do by adding the child to their family profile and completing a mandatory onboarding that explains the built-in safety features. A parent or guardian must be present at the pickup locations for the trip to begin and also have to include a note to the driver that explains the drop off.

Meanwhile, only highly rated drivers who have been invited are allowed to participate. Those drivers are required to complete an education module that includes step-by-step instructions and must be opted into live video streaming so parents can watch the trip in real time, according to Uber.

Uber said it also requires PIN verification for every Uber Kids trip, and says all recordings will be encrypted and not available to the driver, and will use sensors and GPS data to detect if the ride goes off course, stops unexpectedly, or ends early.

Drivers who are willing to adhere to those rules to shuttle kids will get a pay bump for the effort, according to Uber. Eligible drivers will earn $7 more on every Uber Kids trip compared to a standard one, the company says on the dedicated Uber Kids web page. Drivers will receive an extra $20 for the first Uber Kids ride they complete.

The extra compensation underscores a key challenge Uber faces as it expands into this younger age group — how to convince drivers to take on that added responsibility. If the program does expand it could eventually compete with existing transportation services such as HopSkipDrive and Zum.

Uber opened its ride-hailing service to minors in 2023 when it launched Uber for Teens, although the company had conducted early pilots several years prior. As the program expanded nationwide, Uber introduced a live video streaming feature.

news.author: Emily Steel, Kalley Huang, Ryan Mac, and Tripp Mickle
news.content_snippet: The Nvidia co-founder's belittling behavior toward employees goes back decades. It once led to a confidential settlement agreement …
news.summary_en: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly utilized aggressive management tactics, allegedly stating that as employees achieve financial independence due to the company's soaring market cap, humiliation becomes the primary tool to ensure continued high-intensity output. This governance philosophy has triggered internal concerns regarding organizational cohesion and long-term talent retention.
